text:
amy: Heads-up: starting ~02:10 UTC eu-west3 GPU attach rate dropped to ~30% success. Lots of pods Pending and NVMe IOPS on several hosts spiking to 300k r/s.
raj: Any obvious errors in kube events or dmesg?
luca: saw a correlation with the ephemeral-cleaner cron firing right when an etcd leader flip happened. Cleaner restarted a bunch of workers and many tried to delete large tempdirs on the same rack at once.
sre-bot: [alert] ephemeral-cleaner-iops-surge (region=eu-west3, severity=P2) — firing 02:12 UTC :rotating_light:
amy: paste of a representative dmesg snippet:```
[4024681200.123] nvme nvme0: I/O 0x7f failed, status: 0x2 
[4024681200.124] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 1048576
[4024681201.001] ata1: link is slow to respond
```
raj: cleaner config? maybe it doesn't rate-limit per-host.
luca: current job runs: `ephemeral-cleaner --concurrency=12 --shard=auto --lock-store=etcd --scan-interval=5m` — concurrency is cluster-wide so shards rebalanced after leader flip, ended up concentrating work on ~10 nodes.
amy: impact: GPU provisioning controller blocked waiting on attach; attach-controller logs show repeated `device busy` and `timeout waiting for device` errors.
marco: quick mitigation: scale cleaner down for eu-west3 and add a per-node concurrency cap. We can patch job with `--concurrency=2 --per-node-limit=1` while we triage.
amy: did a quick mitigation: `kubectl -n infra scale job/ephemeral-cleaner --replicas=0 --context=eu-west3` (temporary pause). I also cordoned two worst-hit hosts to let attachments drain.
sre-oncall: monitoring: IOPS dropped back to normal within 3 minutes of pause and GPU attach success climbed to 98% :thumbsup:
raj: rollback/long-term: moving lock persistence for janitors to redis/session locks that support automatic session failover would avoid multi-worker rally after etcd leader changes. Also implement jittered backoff on shard migration.
luca: agree. Another durable fix: add deterministic shard-to-host mapping so leader flips don't trigger global reshuffle.
marco: we should also add a runtime circuit breaker: if host NVMe 1s IOPS > 200k, mark host readonly for cleaner ops for 10m.
amy: filed infra-ops ticket #INFRA-8421 with the mitigations and proposed config changes. Assigning to eng-infra + eng-sre for follow-up.
raj: action items: (1) implement per-node limits + backoff (2) design redis-backed lock store (3) add nvme iops circuit-breaker and safe-mode for cleaner (4) run small-scale canary in eu-west3 next low-traffic window.
luca: also capture timelines and attach grafana dashboard snapshots to the ticket.
sre-bot: incident annotated: ephemeral-cleaner-iops-surge — mitigation=paused cleaner, draining worst hosts, monitoring=green.
amy: thanks all. Re-enable cleaner after we merge per-node limit patch and run canary.
marco: noting cost impact: paused cleaner increased ephemeral disk retention by ~12h in eu-west3 — small storage cost but better than production GPU failures.
raj: comms: I'll add a short note to #incidents and ping a few affected customers.
amy: closing thread once ticket has PR + canary results. :white_check_mark:
